chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al-Abbas from Ali ibn Asbat from Sulayman ibn Abi Zaynab from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
My father used to say: 'If I had a path to my house from Mina, I would not enter Mecca.'

key_terms.مِنًى: A valley near Mecca, central to Hajj rituals

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about entering Mecca from Mina?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), used to say that if he had a direct path to his residence from Mina, he would not enter the city of Mea. This highlights the practice of entering Mecca specifically for the rituals of Hajj rather than for general residence or other purposes, emphasizing the spiritual focus of the pilgrimage. In the context of Chapter 20 of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* regarding the departure from Mina, this hadith underscores the principle of *Nafar* (departure) and the intentionality of movement during Hajj, distinguishing between the sacred status of Mina as a place of worship and Mecca as a city of habitation.
